title: Ch-N-N
hookLine: chen, grace; chanun, gracious, in the thirteen attributes

lines: NOT A FACE: A LIST OF NAMES.
cards: The first tablets lie broken at the foot of the mountain, smashed after the golden calf. Moses makes a bold request: "I beseech thee, shew me thy glory." The answer is no, and yes.
No face. But God will pass by while Moses stands hidden in a cleft of the rock, and God will call out names. So Moses climbs again, carrying two new stone tablets.
When it happens, he doesn't see a shape. He hears a list. And right beside mercy in that list stands today's root.

teach.b: Ch-N-N. Chet, nun, nun. Chen, grace, favor.
Chanun, gracious. Turn it four ways. First, an earlier verse.
As the flood story opens, the world has gone bad, and then comes a short line: "But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD." Grace there is chen.

Notice the order: the verse gives no reason first; only after it does the text call Noah a just man. Some readers hear that as the shape of grace: favor that arrives before anyone earns it. Second, back on the mountain.

God passes by and proclaims: "The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth." Merciful is rachum, from yesterday's root. Gracious is chanun, from today's.
The two stand side by side, as if one needs the other.
Third, the priestly blessing from a few days ago, one line further on: "The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee." The same root, asked for every time it's said.
Fourth, the list said aloud, which you met in year two.
Tradition counts the qualities Moses heard as thirteen attributes, and congregations chant them together on fast days and in the season of the High Holy Days.
A people asking to be forgiven reaches for the words God used just after the golden calf. So grace in this root isn't a reward. It's the extra that's given when nothing is owed.

how: Jews chant the thirteen attributes of mercy, drawn from Exodus 34:6–7, aloud on fast days and during the High Holy Days, and the priestly blessing asks that God 'be gracious unto thee'.

o: a debt that must be paid back later
forgiveness given after a punishment is served
grace: favor given freely, more than is owed

p: found grace in the eyes of the LORD

s: Genesis gives a reason before it says Noah found grace
"But Noah found grace" comes first; only afterward is he called just.
in Exodus 34:6, gracious stands right beside merciful
rachum and chanun, side by side.
the priestly blessing asks God to be gracious

games.q: you're Moses, after the golden calf, on the mountain again. you ask: shew me thy glory. what do you get?
o: a full view of God's face.
God passes by and calls out names: merciful and gracious.
games.why: no face. a list: "The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious." tradition counts thirteen attributes in it.

practice: Look ahead at the rest of your day for a moment when someone is owed exactly nothing from you: the driver trying to merge, the slow cashier, the one who apologized badly.

Decide now to give a little more than the rule requires, room, patience, a real thank-you, a pass, and see it happen. If you pray, you can ask, in the words of the blessing, that God be gracious to you, and to them.

wordCard.voice: Ch-N-N. Chet, nun, nun: chen, grace, the favor Noah found, and chanun, gracious, standing beside merciful in the attributes. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: grace. On the mountain, it stands right beside mercy. See you again tomorrow.
